sources.headline: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
sources.text: Vladimir Putin has said Russia will use all weapons at his disposal if it considers its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad to have come under direct attack.The Russian president insisted that Moscow was "not threatening anyone" and merely responding to statements by Western leaders that it was preparing for war in 2029 or 2030.Throughout this week, Russia has accused Nato of preparing to blockade its territory, which borders Lithuania and Poland, warning that it would even be prepared to use nuclear weapons if the West tried to cut off Kaliningrad from the rest of Russia.Nato has sought to calm the situation, stressing that it was a defensive alliance and urging Moscow to stop its "nuclear threats".Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months. Last week alone, Poland said a Russian helicopter had strayed into its territory adjacent to Kaliningrad and Lithuania said its population felt "constantly threatened" by Russia, in part because of drones entering the nation's airspace.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes.In a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum, Putin told his audience that he believed that international conflicts were highly likely to continue, but would get better as "Western hegemony" weakened.Although the Russian leader himself began the full-scale war in Ukraine in February 2022, he again blamed the West for provoking the invasion, arguing that Moscow had simply been forced to defend itself and take up arms.He also insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea."Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," he said.Putin admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war.Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since the war in Ukraine started in 2022. Other civilian infrastructure is also regularly hit, with a key bridge in Kyiv attacked by drones on Thursday.Putin also accused the West of instigating other conflicts."If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation, in this case we are talking about Kaliningrad but possibly some other territories, of course the issue of use by the Russian Federation of all arms at the disposal of our country will inevitably and immediately be on the agenda," he said.He accused Nato of holding naval manoeuvres in the Baltic Sea that he argued represented serious threats to Kaliningrad. If the territory came under Western blockade, he said Russia would be prepared to use all means and forces, including nuclear."We are not threatening anyone. We do not intend to attack anyone in 2029, in 2030, in 2050. But if we come across an aggression we will have to respond. Citizens of European countries should be fully aware of that."He added that while he was aware of the nuclear capabilities of countries such as the UK and France, the weapons at its disposal were unparalleled. Western officials have long feared that, rather than invading Kaliningrad, Russia would use the relatively small distance between the exclave and ally Belarus - known as the Suwalki Gap - were it to attempt to seize Lithuanian territory by force.Lithuania's prime minister told the BBC last week that his country had made evacuation plans in case Russia invaded and thousands of Nato troops are stationed there.Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte made clear on Wednesday that none of the alliance's "exercises or activities" posed any threat to Moscow and that the Kremlin's messaging was "absolutely not called for and not helpful".Putin spent some time talking about leading countries in the world having armaments at their disposal that could "swipe away all life or at least push the Earth to catastrophic consequences", and said that unfortunately no-one could be sure they would never be used.He drew the analogy of a gun sitting on a theatre stage - if it was hanging there at the start of the show, it would certainly be fired at the end.He appeared to call for the rules of warfare to be rewritten and warned of the increasing risk of artificial intelligence."The automation and digitalisation of warfare leads to its gamification. This leads to degradation and sliding back of humanity to barbarity," he said.

sources.headline: Putin says ‘all weapons at disposal’ if there’s an attack on Russia – as it happened
sources.text:
From 5h agoRussia's Putin confirms 'all weapons at disposal' in case of attack on Russia, but says it would not attack firstIn the Q&A after his speech, Russia’s Putin also got asked about Moscow’s widely reported nuclear threat over Kaliningrad (Europe Live, yesterday).Russian president Vladimir Putin attends a plenary session of the 23d annual meeting of the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow, Russia. Photograph: Maxim Shipenkov/EPAPutin confirms that Russia issued a statement and letters to some embassies on this point.But he claims:
“This is not us threatening, but this is a response to attempts to threaten us.”
He continues:
“These statements, statements by the western politicians and European politicians about the need and possibility and preparation for the war with Russia in 2029 and 2030.
It’s not us saying these words, but we hear it from the other side, constantly.”
He eventually confirms that “if it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation – in this case we mean Kaliningrad, but may be some other territories as well – of course, naturally, immediately what will be on the agenda is the use … of all weapons that we are the disposal of our country.”He says that with Nato a potential adversary “exceeding us,” Russia would not have “many means to counter such a threat,” and would need to use its “competitive advantages.”But Putin says that the risk of using nuclear weapons is only serious if Nato’s threats against Russia are serious.And then he goes on a rant about taking his words out of context, so let’s quote him in full:
“I think that this constant increased tension by many European countries; it has to do with a great deterioration of economic and domestic political situation in the countries. Look at their economy, what’s happening in terms of social policy and living standards of citizens in major European countries. Amid such conditions, they have to shift the focus of attention of their citizens from domestic issues towards outside issues.
Now, I have to respond to the questions that you asked me, and I think that they were waiting for us to respond.
Right now, they will cut it out of context, and they will abuse and exploit this notion that Russia is threatening us with nuclear weapons to distract the attention of their citizens from the fact that they are conducting their own aggressive policy against Russia, that they’re pushing their citizens towards a dangerous line towards confrontation against Russia.
We’re not threatening anyone. We do not intend to attack anyone in 2029, in 2030, in 2050, but if we come across an aggression, we will have to respond.
The citizens of the European countries should be fully aware of that and make the distinction between our position and the position of incumbent governments of their countries.”
Curiously, a moment later, he also appears to play down tensions a bit as he says “I do not think we are going to conduct strikes on the territory of countries procuring weapons for Ukraine, but this is a threat, and we are monitoring it closely.”Key events5h agoClosing summary5h agoRussia's Putin confirms 'all weapons at disposal' in case of attack on Russia, but says it would not attack first5h agoPutin says conflicts likely to continue and Russia was 'forced' into war in Ukraine6h agoEurope 'not at peace today' amid growing Russian malign hybrid attacks, Nato chief warns6h agoGermany preparing for 'major hybrid attacks' and ready to respond 'swiftly,' chancellor Merz says7h agoFrench high school protests escalate with reported violence7h agoSikorski says Poland would welcome Britain back to EU 'with open arms'8h agoUkraine made net gains in September with counteroffensive push against Russia8h agoJoint EU–Ukraine statement says they have 'identified means' on budget shortfall9h agoFinland investigates suspected break-ins at MPs homes9h agoA determined show of unity amid growing tensions with Russia - snap analysis9h ago'I hope Putin gets the message' as he is 'failing to intimidate us,' Rutte says9h ago'We see Russia testing us across Europe,' and 'must be prepared for hostile actions,' Nato chief says9h agoRussia 'poses rapidly increasing threat' to Nato, Dutch PM says9h agoRussia's 'violent revisionism' challenging Europe's peace, Merz warns9h agoRussian drone hits grounds of nuclear research facility in Kyiv9h agoRutte, Merz, Jetten about to speak at joint press conference in Germany10h agoGermany's Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims national team are ‘not white enough’10h agoEU countries, Britain hold call on possible release of reserve diesel stacks11h agoKyiv Independent editor: ‘Our readers want Russia to suffer but we can’t be propagandists’11h agoTwo Russian drones hit a major bridge in Kyiv12h agoRussia expels Hungary's diplomats in retaliation to Budapest's move earlier this month12h agoUK adopts new sanctions on Russia over Ukraine war12h agoRussian drone hits school in Kyiv13h agoUkraine hits oil facility in Russia's Samara region despite pressure from Trump13h agoItaly, Poland extend suspensions of Schengen rules to fight irregular migration13h agoEstonia bans transit of Russian, Belarusian grain through its territory14h agoMorning opening: Russia continues strikes on Ukraine as Zelenskyy makes a frontline visitClosing summaryJakub KrupaAnd, on that note, we will be closing the blog for today.

sources.headline: Putin warns Russia will use ‘all weapons’ in arsenal if any of its territory is attacked
Putin warns West Russia will use 'all weapons' if Kaliningrad threatened
sources.text: Posted Fri 2 Oct 2026 at 5:15amFri 2 Oct 2026 at 5:15amRussian leader Vladimir Putin says he has "competitive advantages'' and will use them. (Reuters: Ramil Sitdikov)In short: Russian President Vladimir Putin says he is prepared to use "all weapons" at Moscow's disposal if the West threatens the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.Moscow has previously sent a diplomatic note to NATO warning against military build-up around the Baltic.Mr Putin also said Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure had shaved 1 per cent off Russia's GDP.Vladimir Putin says the world is living through a dangerous moment and has warned the West not to escalate a stand-off over Ukraine by threatening the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has made clear it will defend with nuclear weapons if necessary.Locked in a war in Ukraine, which he said Russia had no choice but to launch to safeguard its own security, Mr Putin said Moscow had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully.But he reiterated that Russia would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its most westerly territory — Kaliningrad, which is wedged between Poland and Lithuania — were threatened."If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation — in this case, we are referring to Kaliningrad, and perhaps other territories as well — the question of the Russian Federation deploying all the weapons at our country's disposal will, of course, inevitably and immediately be on the agenda," Mr Putin told the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow."This is inevitable," he said.Mr Putin said Russia realised it would be facing "an enemy [NATO] twice our size". "And we will have to make use of our competitive advantages in this struggle. Yes, of course, France and Britain are nuclear powers — we understand that perfectly well and are fully aware of it," he said."But no-one else possesses the kind of weapons that Russia has today. That is our competitive advantage."Nuclear warningMr Putin's comments followed a diplomatic note which NATO said this week it had received from Russia, warning the Western military alliance it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if NATO attempted to cut off Russia's Baltic exclave.Russia's warning highlighted Moscow's urgent concern at what it has presented as a growing NATO threat to Kaliningrad, a heavily militarised Russian territory that is slightly bigger than the US state of Connecticut. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance had responded by emphasising that it was a defensive alliance and that nuclear threats were not helpful.Mr Putin conceded that Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries across Russia had cost Russia 1 per cent of its gross domestic product (GDP).But he said Russia was now responding to Ukraine in kind.Reuters

sources.headline: ‘Fatal point of no return’: Putin warns against use of nukes amid global tensions
sources.text: Russian President Vladimir Putin attends Valdai International Discussion Club in Moscow (Picture credit: Reuters)Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday warned that the world was living through a dangerous moment, saying escalating international conflicts could reach a “fatal point of no return” and stressing that weapons of mass destruction must never be used.Speaking at the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow, Putin said the world’s leading powers possessed arsenals capable of destroying all life or reducing the Earth to a “catastrophic state”.He urged countries to recognise how quickly escalating retaliation could lead to an irreversible situation.“We must realise that the moment when nothing can be changed any longer may come very quickly and unexpectedly for everyone. The logic of escalating, increasingly harsh retaliatory measures leads to a fatal point of no return,” Putin said.“At the heart of this escalation lie arrogance and overconfidence. This is a path to the brink of the abyss. All the more so today, when the arsenals of the world’s leading powers contain weapons capable of destroying all life or, at the very least, reducing the Earth to a catastrophic state. Can we be certain that these weapons will never be used? Well, of course not. We must bear this in mind and avoid such an outcome.”Putin warns of Western role in Ukraine conflictPutin said Ukraine would not be able to carry out attacks deep inside Russia without Western technical support, arguing that such assistance amounted to direct involvement in the conflict.He said Russia viewed attempts to use Ukraine as a proxy to fight Russia as a threat. Putin also said Moscow was not planning to attack factories in other countries that manufacture weapons for Ukraine, but warned that Russia's military and intelligence services needed to closely monitor them.“We are not going to attack tomorrow enterprises in countries which supply weapons to Ukraine, but that's a threat,” Putin said.Putin also said Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries had cost Russia 1% of its gross domestic product.He said Ukraine had “partially achieved its objectives” through the attacks, but added that Russia was responding in kind.He further said Ukraine had damaged more than 100 Russian vessels in the Black Sea and that Moscow was now responding.Russia issues warning over KaliningradPutin said Russia would consider using the full range of weapons in its arsenal if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad came under threat. He maintained that Russia did not plan to attack anyone but would respond to aggression.“We are not going to attack anyone, but will respond if we face aggression,” Putin said.Kaliningrad is a Russian territory on the Baltic Sea separated from mainland Russia by other countries and located between Nato members Poland and Lithuania. The region has become a focus of tensions between Moscow and the alliance.In a separate development on Thursday, the Kremlin said Russia's recent letter to Nato on Kaliningrad should not be viewed as confrontational. The document accused the alliance of pursuing a “dangerous and reckless course” carrying “high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict”.Putin also said Russia was not threatening European countries and did not plan to attack them.“We are not threatening anyone and we do not plan to attack any European countries, not in 2030, not in 2050,” he said.Putin says global conflicts likely to continuePutin said international conflicts were likely to continue as the global order undergoes fundamental changes, although he said the situation would improve as what he described as Western hegemony waned.“Regardless of which scenario unfolds globally in the coming years, the continuation of international conflicts is, unfortunately, highly likely. This is due in part to the fact that ongoing fundamental shifts—and the opportunities they present—fuel ambitions and a willingness to take risks for the sake of a seemingly massive payoff,” Putin said.He again stressed the need to avoid catastrophic scenarios.Putin also said Russia supported a possible trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, although he said an agenda for such talks would first need to be worked out.On the Middle East, Putin said he hoped the Strait of Hormuz would remain open to shipping and that sanctions on Iran would be lifted. He also said Russia's proposals to deliver enriched uranium from Iran to Russia remained valid.Putin said Russia remained interested in cooperation with Japan but was concerned about what he described as the country's militarisation.He added that Japanese companies continued to operate in Russia and that Moscow supported them and others working with Russia.He also criticised military drills and arrests of Russian vessels as forms of escalation and said Russia had a competitive advantage in defending itself.

sources.headline: World living through a dangerous moment, says Putin, warns West not to escalate
sources.text: MOSCOW - President Vladimir Putin said on Oct 1 the world was living through a dangerous moment and warned the West not to escalate a standoff over Ukraine by threatening the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which Moscow has said it will defend with nuclear weapons if necessary.Locked in a war in Ukraine which he said Russia had no choice but to launch in order to safeguard its own security, Putin said Russia had no plans to attack any European country and wanted to coexist peacefully.But he reiterated that Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its most westerly territory - Kaliningrad, which is wedged between Poland and Lithuania - was threatened.“If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation – in this case, we are referring to Kaliningrad, and perhaps other territories as well – the question of the Russian Federation deploying all the weapons at our country’s disposal will, of course, inevitably and immediately be on the agenda,” Putin told the Valdai Forum of international Russia experts in Moscow.“This is inevitable,” he said.Putin said Russia realised it would be facing “an enemy (NATO) twice our size.”“And we will have to make use of our competitive advantages in this struggle. Yes, of course, France and Britain are nuclear powers – we understand that perfectly well and are fully aware of it,” he said.“But no one else possesses the kind of weapons that Russia has today. That is our competitive advantage.”Nuclear warningPutin’s comments followed a diplomatic note which NATO said this week it had received from Russia, warning the Western military alliance it would be ready to resort to nuclear weapons if NATO attempted to cut off Russia’s Baltic exclave.Russia’s warning highlighted Moscow’s urgent concern at what it has presented as a growing NATO threat to Kaliningrad, a heavily militarised Russian territory that is slightly bigger than the US state of Connecticut.NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said the alliance had responded by emphasising that it was a defensive alliance and that nuclear threats were not helpful.Relations, already dire since Putin’s decision to send troops into Ukraine in 2022, have worsened this year, with European governments accusing Moscow of stepping up a “hybrid war” on the continent through acts including sabotage and arson.Russia denies that, and rejects repeated statements by Western politicians that it is gearing up for a possible military attack on a NATO country.Putin warned that cycles of escalation in international conflict could quickly lead to dangerous scenarios.“We must realise that the moment when nothing can be changed any longer may come very quickly and unexpectedly for everyone. The logic of escalating, increasingly harsh retaliatory measures leads to a fatal point of no return,” he said.“At the heart of this escalation lie arrogance and overconfidence. This is a path to the brink of the abyss. All the more so today, when the arsenals of the world’s leading powers contain weapons capable of destroying all life or, at the very least, reducing the Earth to a catastrophic state,” Putin said.“Can we be certain that these weapons will never be used? Well, of course not. We must bear this in mind and avoid such an outcome,” he added.Putin, who said he was ready for a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump if a proper agenda was worked out first, ruled out the idea of stopping Russian strikes on Ukrainian targets in the Black Sea area, while conceding that Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries across Russia had cost Russia 1% of its gross domestic product (GDP).He said Russia was now responding to Ukraine in kind.But while he cast Western help to Kyiv when it came to launching deep strikes inside Russia as a future threat, he said Moscow was not planning to attack arms factories in Europe which supplied Ukraine “tomorrow.” REUTERS

sources.headline: Russia launches major attack on Ukraine’s energy grid, causing power cuts
Several regions of Ukraine hit by power cuts after Russian strikes, grid operator says
sources.text:
Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure have caused power cuts in several regions, grid operator Ukrenergo said on Thursday, urging consumers to limit usage.
Recent attacks have caused outages from the Kharkiv region in the east, Chernihiv and Sumy in the north, to Rivne in the northwest and Kirovohrad in central Ukraine, it said.
"Where security conditions currently allow, emergency repair and restoration work is already under way," a statement read.
"Energy workers are doing everything possible to restore power to all disconnected consumers as quickly as possible."
The cuts come after Russia said on Wednesday that it deliberately targeted Ukraine's energy infrastructure with drones and missiles in the capital, Kyiv, and nearby region.
Kyiv said it was Moscow's opening salvo in an expected campaign to try to knock out heating and power as winter approaches.
A recent increase in strikes has prompted fears about another winter with little or no power or heating, after similar attacks last year when temperatures plunged to -20C.
Some emergency power outages were implemented in Kyiv on Wednesday night.
Ukrenergo urged domestic consumers to switch "intensive energy use" to daytime hours and said "economical" use was needed in some areas in the evening.
Hourly power outages and capacity limits for industrial consumers were not currently being implemented, it added.
But the operator still urged a reduction in use at night, particularly in Kyiv and the surrounding regions.
Moscow's forces also hit a school in Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, with Russia increasing strikes on the capital as it braces for another winter of war.
Children and teachers were already in a shelter, Kyiv said, reporting no casualties.
"Russian scumbags continue attacking life across our country, Ukrainian children and our schools," Zelenskyy said in a post on X, publishing footage of the building with blown-out windows.
Zelenskyy has repeatedly appealed to Ukraine's allies for more military support, including US-made interceptors to combat Russia's powerful ballistic missiles.
"Every interceptor missile truly saves lives," he said on Wednesday. "And the closer we get to winter, the more of this protection we need."
Strikes on Odesa
Meanwhile, one person was injured in the southern port city of Odesa overnight into Thursday, after a Russian attack struck a business centre sparking a fire and damaging the roof and the facades of two other buildings, local authorities said.
The blast shattered windows and partially destroyed walls on the fifth floor, Odesa Regional State Emergency Service said.
"A fire broke out at the scene and was extinguished by firefighters. Unfortunately, one person was injured,” Oleksander Kolosyuk, a representative of the State Emergency Service of Ukraine, said.
Russia launched 107 drones at Ukraine overnight into Thursday, including 63 jet-powered drones, Ukraine’s Air Force said in its daily report.
Attacks were recorded at 11 locations, while debris from downed drones fell at four.
The Air Force said the attack was still ongoing, with more drones in the air.
Additional sources • AP, AFP
